messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw a TTFT spike on /generate after the kernel-selector change rolled last night. baseline was ~40ms, now some p95s are 120–200ms.
jonathan: Ugh. Is it for cold requests or warm ones?
maria: Mostly cold. Warm requests still look fine. The KV cache hit-rate dropped for a subset of long-conversation flows.
lee: Could be the new kernel choice favoring lower-latency batch throughput but slower single-stream kernels.
perfbot: Automated profile attached: kernel_select_v2 applied on 2024-11-01 03:12UTC. Top samples: decode_total=95ms, kernel_time=88ms, memcpy=12ms, scheduling=20ms.
anika: Can you paste a short token-level breakdown? we need TTFT vs decode attribution for the dashboard panels.
maria: Sure — sample from one impacted request (shortened):
```
TTFT_total: 190ms
  - dispatch/queue: 22ms
  - kernel_select: 6ms
  - kernel_invoke: 110ms
  - decode_postproc: 30ms
  - kv_lookup: 12ms
  - memcpy: 10ms
```
jonathan: kernel_invoke 110ms is alarming for a single token. which kernel variant?
maria: The selector picked quant_q2f32_blocking (new heur), which is optimized for batched throughput. For single-stream it has extra lock contention we didn't account for.
lee: That explains cold TTFT. Batching heuristics probably grouped tiny requests into a pseudo-batch that triggers the slower path.
kevin: Should we attribute kernel time to "decode" vs "TTFT" in metrics? Right now kernel_time is lumped into total.
anika: We discussed splitting: TTFT = time_before_first_token_emitted; decode = CPU/text postprocessing; kernel_time attribution fields like kernel_time_decode vs kernel_time_kv could be emitted by runtime.
maria: I'd prefer emitting per-token tags: token.ttft_ms, token.decode_ms, token.kernel_ms, token.kv_ms. Store as histograms.
perfbot: Suggestion: add two new Prom labels: kernel_phase=(decode|kv|kv_lookup|dispatch). Emit kernel_time_seconds with kernel_phase label.
jonathan: That would let dashboards show p50/p95 per-phase and per-route. Also we can detect regressions where kernel_time_kv jumps.
lee: Practical note: minimize cardinality — only the phase label and route/model tag. No prompt-id or user id.
kevin: For attribution we might need lightweight stack traces sampled on top kernel calls to confirm which GPU kernels are slow.
anika: Agreed. Also add a counter for cache_miss->full_kv_fetch to quickly surface KV-related TTFT regressions.
maria: Action items: 1) runtime: emit kernel_time_seconds with kernel_phase label (maria). 2) metrics: add histograms and per-route dashboard panels for TTFT vs decode vs kernel (jonathan). 3) infra: add nightly regression check on p95 TTFT per-route (lee).
jonathan: I'll open the dashboards ticket and add example panels: TTFT_p95 trend, kernel_phase breakdown stacked, kv_miss_rate.
maria: Created issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4127 — I attached the profile and sample traces. Please add link to PR once kernel-phase labels are in. :thumbsup:
lee: Thanks — putting a canary rollback on the kernel selector change until we get a fix out. :eyes: 
kevin: Will probe with microbenchmarks for single-stream kernels and report numbers.
perfbot: Nightly perf alert rule updated: alert if route:/generate TTFT_p95 increases by >25% vs baseline.
anika: Nice. If we standardize token-level fields, the Optimize team can add recommendations (e.g., prefer kernel_x for low-concurrency flows).
maria: OK thanks everyone — ping me if you need the raw perf traces.
